critical_evidence.evidence: The California smog VIR dated 10/14/2026 shows an OBDII pass. Engine-bay photos show a stock intake. One owner with a dealer-serviced history. None of this rules out a flash-and-revert, so the PPI should read the ECU software ID and flash counter.

There is no reported water pump, thermostat housing or coolant service entry in the Carfax. The selling dealer's own RO 104200 marks 'cooling system' and 'engine leaks' as pass. That is a seller-side check, not an independent inspection or a replacement record.

documentation.rationale: Both halves are present. On identity and terms: VIN, clean guaranteed title, an itemised $19,065.15 OTD sheet and a 1-owner Carfax. On maintenance: 10 service entries, the full 5-page dealer RO, a smog VIR, 19 photos and a video. What is missing: no cooling-system records, brake fluid last reported in 2019, and nothing reported between 11/2023 and 10/2026.

condition.rationale: The dealer RO records 53 of 54 points passed, including clutch operation. Front and rear rotors are newly replaced. Tires are DOT 2022 at 7-8/32, and the car passed smog. Observed defects are driver-door dings with a crease, hood and roof water-spot etching, and rotors described as 'severely warped/scorched' despite 7 mm pads. The inspection is the seller's own, and the car sat nearly unused for about 3 years.

price_value.rationale: The $16,995 selling price ($17,117 with doc fee) is above the $15,354-$16,130 fair-value estimate. The Roseville 2015 GTI S peer asks $14,495, though it has higher mileage. The recall and the paint recon are still to be confirmed.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, sits inside the ideal budget band, and is available now. Jason's mechanic works on VWs, and the hatchback gives everyday usefulness. Manual GTIs resell easily within a 6-24 month window.

logistics.rationale: Oxnard, CA is a moderate distance from Carmel, and the car is already California-smogged and registered. A PPI is possible but only through a borrowed-car arrangement to a local shop.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: A typical example: base S trim in a common colour. The manual and the plaid interior are the expected GTI traits. No Performance Pack differential is indicated.

Observed: the driver door has a crease and dings, and the hood and roof show water-spot etching. These are going to PDR and paint with no ETA, and there is no invoice yet.
Observed: only about 837 miles in nearly 3 years since 11/2023, with no reported oil service in that period. The car may have sat parked under trees.

Unverified: brake fluid has not been reported flushed since 10/2019 (ask; test moisture at PPI).

ppi_focus: Water-pump and thermostat housing for weeping or pink crust; pressure-test the cooling system
Clutch slip test (4th/5th gear pull at low rpm), engagement height and dual-mass flywheel noise
All four brake calipers: slide pins, piston retraction, drag after a drive (IR temperature check), and brake fluid moisture
VCDS/OBDeleven scan for stored codes, ECU software ID and flash counter (tune or revert evidence), and misfire counters
Paint-meter reading on the hood, roof and driver door after the dealer's recon; check the quality of the refinish
Fuel tank and recall area; confirm recall 24V110 is closed in the VW system
Underside after 3 years of sitting: bushings, CV boots, exhaust, oil leaks at the timing cover and oil pan
PCV valve and rear main area for oil leaks, since the car sat with little use
Alignment and tire wear pattern; inspect the curb-rashed wheel
Check for any water-intrusion signs in the cabin, as the car was parked under trees
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a written recall 24V110 completion record, plus a body/paint invoice with clean after photos and sensible paint-meter readings.
Up: a clean independent PPI with no caliper drag, no water-pump weep, a healthy clutch and a stock ECU software ID.
Up: a price concession toward the fair-value range.
Down: evidence of a flashed and reverted tune, clutch slip, an active coolant weep, or a seized caliper.
Down: the dealer refusing to complete the recall, or poor-quality paint work hiding more than the stated dings.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, one-owner manual GTI in California, within the ideal budget band, fits the enthusiast-bridge brief directly. It is a hatchback with an easy resale path, and Jason's VW-capable mechanic can maintain it. Accelerated-bridge mode still means the recall, paint work and an independent PPI should be settled before money moves.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax establishes one California owner since 2018 with a clean guaranteed title and regular Ventura VW service through 11/2023. The dealer's full RO 104200 shows 53 of 54 inspection points passed, new front and rear rotors, matching 2022 Michelins at 7-8/32, and a 10/14/2026 smog pass. Observed issues are an open recall 24V110 that is not on the RO, rotors described as severely warped and scorched despite 7 mm pads, and driver-door dings with hood and roof etching that are going to PDR and paint with no invoice yet. Use was nearly nil from 11/2023 to 10/2026 (about 837 miles), with no reported service in that window. There is no reported water pump, thermostat housing or brake-fluid service since 2019, and absence in the Carfax does not prove the work was skipped. The $16,995 selling price sits above the $15,354-$16,130 fair-value estimate. Tune risk looks low on the smog pass and photos, but an ECU software read is still open. A PPI is permitted only under a borrowed-car agreement.
